findings.title: WHOAMI competes with HUMAN as semantic home
findings.summary: Wings4 recorded a human directive that useful WHOAMI context/data must be absorbed into HUMAN so WHOAMI does not remain competing canon.

evidence.label: DEC-W4-047
evidence.excerpt: HUMAN must become the semantic home of useful WHOAMI context/data; WHOAMI must not remain competing semantic canon.

evidence.label: Q-064
evidence.excerpt: SkillsMachine evaluates and implements locally after consulting its HUMAN and Q&A; Wings4 does not mutate SkillsMachine.

evidence.label: Transfer package
evidence.excerpt: STATUS ready for SkillsMachine ORCHESTRATOR review; THIS_IS_NOT_AN_EXECUTOR_PROMPT=YES.

findings.impact: If left unresolved, operators and AI sessions may treat WHOAMI as competing doctrine, weakening HUMAN authority and creating duplicate continuity semantics.
alternatives: A. Retire WHOAMI after dependency validation
B. Reduce WHOAMI to a minimal pointer to HUMAN
C. Retain WHOAMI temporarily with explicit deprecation
findings.recommendation: Deliver the prepared transfer to SkillsMachine ORCHESTRATOR; prefer minimal pointer to HUMAN if local dependencies allow; require return evidence before Wings4 resync.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.

evidence.label: Active BATON
evidence.excerpt: SkillsMachine-local dirty workstreams remain SkillsMachine-owned and out of this transfer scope.

evidence.label: Transfer exclusions
evidence.excerpt: Excluded: DocumentConsistencyAudit allowlist change; SMDI harness patch; transcript Skill placement; session-close retention.

evidence.label: Q-064 / compiled interpretation
evidence.excerpt: Unrelated SkillsMachine dirty workstreams remain out of scope.

findings.impact: Mixing unrelated dirty scopes risks invalid attribution, accidental combined commits and delayed product/demo readiness inside SkillsMachine.
alternatives: Disposition each dirty path independently under SkillsMachine governance
Freeze SMDI candidate until separate review
Postpone all unrelated dirty work while WHOAMI→HUMAN proceeds alone
findings.recommendation: Keep dirty technical workstreams out of the WHOAMI transfer. Require SkillsMachine-local independent disposition before any SkillsMachine EXECUTOR authorization.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.

findings.title: Updater maturity exceeds real-consumer proof
findings.summary: Representative synthesis of Wings4-held SkillsMachine readiness notes: updater LAB evidence is stronger than proven real-consumer acceptance. Marked noncanonical because this Ring0 build did not re-open SkillsMachine files.

evidence.label: Wings4 product relationship decision
evidence.excerpt: Optional product integration for reusable Skills/GRCs is distinct from proven consumer rollout.

evidence.label: Delivery model
evidence.excerpt: Reports and architecture alone are not product functionality; live operable proof is required.

findings.impact: Over-claiming distribution readiness could create false management confidence before a real consumer pilot exists.
alternatives: Treat updater as proven only at LAB/fixture level until real-consumer evidence returns
Open a separate governed SkillsMachine product slice after local readiness
Postpone distribution claims from Wings4 demos
findings.recommendation: In Wings4 demos, state updater readiness cautiously and keep real-consumer proof as a SkillsMachine-local future gate.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.
